consensus_summary: Living water primarily symbolizes the Holy Spirit given by Jesus (explicitly via John 7:39), tightly linked with eternal life/salvation that quenches spiritual thirst; secondary or overlapping alternatives include baptism, God as fountain, Christ as giver, eschatological restoration, and (as minority) the word/gospel.
book_summary: The Spirit and word of God going out to give life.
consensus_core_identification: The Holy Spirit (imparting eternal life/salvation from Christ)
book_core_identification: The Spirit and word of God going out to give life
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats the word/gospel as a minority alternative or secondary extension; the book elevates it to co-primary status alongside the Spirit, expanding the core identification beyond the settled Johannine referent.
material_contradiction: None; the book retains the Spirit as part of the identification and does not deny the consensus primary referent.
rationale: Minimum cores share the Spirit as life-giving agent (preserving the consensus category anchored in John 7), but the book materially broadens by conjoining 'word of God' as equal core element rather than minority alternative. This is boundary refinement (added cases/referents) without replacement or contradiction of the central Spirit identification.
strongest_objection: John 7:39 (the explicit Spirit gloss, not printed) fixes the primary NT referent as the Spirit alone; elevating 'word' lacks direct support from the printed citations and risks diluting the settled consensus.
